title: Le Bristol Paris: Midnight in Paris Hotel Guide
description: Le Bristol Paris on Rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré appears in Woody Allen's Midnight in Paris. Film facts, hotel history and tips for booking a stay.
h1: Le Bristol Paris: the palace hotel from Midnight in Paris
intro: Le Bristol sits on the Rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré and has welcomed guests since 1925. Woody Allen's Midnight in Paris put it on screen as the hotel where a couple from California stays.
filming: In Midnight in Paris (2011), Le Bristol was used for the hotel-room scenes of Gil and Inez on their trip to Paris. Wikipedia lists the hotel among the film's appearances, and travel writers describe it as a location for many of the movie's scenes.
facts: Hippolyte Jammet bought the mansion in 1923 and opened the hotel in April 1925.
The hotel changed hands only once, in 1978, when the Jammet family sold it to the Oetker family.
It is part of Oetker Collection, formerly Oetker Hotels.
Its rooftop swimming pool, designed by the architect Pinnau, resembles the front of a large sailboat.
visit: The hotel has a garden and a pool with views over the Paris rooftops, and the luxury boutiques of Rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré are on the doorstep. Check dates early, as it is a small, popular palace hotel.
